text: FADER publishes a Zoom interview/profile with Zara Larsson timed to the late‑September 2025 release of her album Midnight Sun. The article frames Midnight Sun as a creative breakthrough that arrives after more than a decade in pop, emphasizing that Larsson, now 27, is finally receiving broader recognition. It contrasts her earlier years, when she did not write songs and saw herself mainly as a performer, with the Midnight Sun era, where she describes being far more involved in songwriting, concept, and visuals, saying she has never previously created such a full "world" and "vibe" around a project. The piece characterizes Midnight Sun as an exuberant, maximalist, pleasure‑seeking Swedish pop album with a cohesive feel and a distinctive je ne sais quoi absent from her previous releases. It highlights songs such as "Crush," "Hot & Sexy," and "Puss Puss" as examples of her strong, flirty, unserious point of view. The interview explores the album’s aesthetic inspirations, including Lisa Frank imagery and a viral dolphin meme tied to her earlier hit "Symphony," and notes that she incorporated dolphins into her shows and merchandising. It also reports that Tiffany Pollard appears on "Hot & Sexy," enhancing the playful, referential pop‑culture tone. The article discusses themes of ambition, competition, and Larsson’s long‑standing desire to be "pop’s number one girl," relating these ideas to songs like "The Ambition" and to her experiences being compared to other female pop artists. Overall, FADER presents Midnight Sun as a cohesive, maximalist pop project representing a new, more self‑directed phase in Larsson’s career, with a carefully built visual and conceptual universe informed by internet culture and Swedish pop tradition.

Staged Haze runs a review of Zara Larsson’s album Midnight Sun, released in late September 2025 and described as a concise, sub‑32‑minute collection of nostalgic summer dance‑pop songs that may be her best work yet. The review explains that the album’s central inspiration is Larsson’s Swedish pop heritage and the idea of the Swedish summer where the sun never sets. Citing a Women in Pop interview, it notes that Larsson envisioned the record feeling like a summer night that never ends, so that listeners can access that feeling even in winter. The piece recounts the album’s rollout with singles "Pretty Ugly," "Midnight Sun," and "Crush," describing their sounds and TikTok traction. It emphasizes Larsson’s increased creative involvement, quoting her FADER remark about having never before created a full "world and vibe" and stating that she co‑wrote all of the album’s tracks, which were executive produced by Uzo Emenike (MNEK). The review describes Midnight Sun’s aesthetic world as a Y2K digital fantasy expressed through cover art, styling, and videos, and mentions a merchandising collaboration with Lisa Frank, as well as Tiffany Pollard’s sampled appearance on "Hot & Sexy." The writer observes that while many songs are bright, fun pop reminiscent of Larsson’s past hits, ballads like "Saturn Return" and "The Ambition" reveal more vulnerable themes about adulthood, ambition, and self‑comparison, underlining how the album balances carefree hedonism with reflections on pressure and ambition.

This Switched On Pop Substack post summarizes a podcast interview with Zara Larsson conducted around the release of Midnight Sun and focuses on how Sweden’s extreme seasonal light and dark inform the album’s concept and mood. The article describes Midnight Sun as capturing the tension between euphoric surfaces and underlying melancholy, analogous to Swedes’ intense enjoyment of brief summer light against the backdrop of long, dark winters. In the interview, Larsson explains that the Swedish midnight sun feels like her childhood: summers where it never truly gets dark, she spent long nights outside, and only later realized how unusual this was. She contrasts these bright summers with Sweden’s very dark, cold winters, saying the stark contrast makes people treasure moments of warmth and sunlight, even pausing in the street to turn their faces toward the sun and storing these memories to endure winter. She connects this pattern to her creative life, remarking that summer is for enjoyment while winter is when Swedes retreat to studios and work, shaping how and when she writes and records. Discussing the title track "Midnight Sun," she calls it euphoric and grateful for life, representing freedom from responsibilities and an experience of nature linked to the midnight sun phenomenon. She says she had long wanted to write a song called "Midnight Sun," especially after traveling more and missing Swedish summers, but only did so for this album. Larsson also comments on how remaining in Sweden, rather than moving to Los Angeles, has kept her grounded in this environment, and explains that singing in English rather than Swedish helps her manage emotional vulnerability in songs that mix joy and sadness. The post presents Midnight Sun as deliberately built around the interplay of light and dark, both literal and emotional, rooted in Larsson’s experience of Swedish seasons.

The piece introduces the Capital Buzz series as a behind‑the‑scenes look at how notable records are created and notes that Larsson joins previous guests such as Conan Gray and Chappell Roan. It states that in this episode Larsson speaks candidly about chart performance, owning her masters, and being compared to other female artists, alongside discussing the artistic side of Midnight Sun. In the partial written recap, the track‑by‑track section begins with the title song "Midnight Sun," which Larsson describes as expressing freedom from everyday responsibilities by escaping into nature and embodying the euphoric sensation of the midnight sun. She says the track encapsulates the things she currently loves most in music and in life. The article notes that she goes on in the audio/video to unpack each subsequent song in a similar way, touching on lyrical inspiration, romantic and autobiographical elements, and how individual tracks came together in the studio. It comments that Larsson had long been attracted to the idea of a song called "Midnight Sun" but only realized it on this album, and that she characterizes "The Ambition" as dealing explicitly with career drive and the pressure of chasing big dreams, echoing broader themes of comparison and ambition in her recent public comments. Capital FM frames the episode as an in‑depth look at how Midnight Sun was made, emphasizing Larsson’s increased creative control, ownership of her masters, and clear emotional and thematic intentions for each track.

The Line of Best Fit publishes a feature‑length interview with Zara Larsson that situates the Midnight Sun era within her broader career and highlights the album as her "easiest and truest" music so far. The article describes the song "Midnight Sun" as a strong contender for song of the summer whose streaming and viral success have created a cultural moment even without major US or UK chart placements. It notes a wider "cultural shift" surrounding Larsson, with online buzz, viral clips of her live vocals and music video, and a memorable VMAs appearance in crystallised hibiscus‑flower attire that visually anchors the Midnight Sun aesthetic. The profile traces Larsson’s trajectory from early hits and collaborations like "Lush Life" and "Symphony" through a decade of steady presence to the current phase, arguing that Midnight Sun represents a new, more cohesive artistic realm. In the interview, conducted while she is on tour opening for Tate McRae, Larsson reflects on repeatedly being "rediscovered" by the public and jokes about metaphorically scrambling up the walls of pop stardom, saying she and her team are on the last steps of a hill about to see a beautiful view. text: Rolling Stone 的这篇专辑评测将《Midnight Sun》描述为一张从头到尾保持高能量的 dance-pop 专辑，围绕夏日、漫长白昼与不眠之夜的氛围展开。文章强调主打曲“Midnight Sun”以带有 trance 元素的迷离合唱和高音转音作为高能量开场，整张专辑在“甜”与“辛辣”情绪之间摇摆。评测具体分析了多首歌曲的主题：如“Midnight Sun”“Blue Moon”“Euro Summer”“Puss Puss”中的甜蜜夏日恋情场景，以及“Girl’s Girl”“Pretty Ugly”“The Ambition”“Saturn’s Return”等更具“坏女”“混乱”或自我反思意味的作品。评论认为那些更“凌乱”的时刻最能体现 Larsson 的生命力，整体评价偏正面，称她在这张专辑中逐步找到自己的位置，即便部分桥段较为公式化，仍被形容为比瑞典夏日阳光更耀眼。

EUPHORIA. 的乐评将《Midnight Sun》称为“终极派对唱片”，强调全盘 10 首歌都充满足以随时让人起身跳舞的能量与活力。文章指出专辑在风格上以 dance-pop 为基础，融入 trance、Brazilian funk 和 ballroom 等多样电子与俱乐部音乐元素，同时强调 Zara Larsson 在创作和制作上的亲力亲为，与长期合作伙伴 MNEK 及词曲作者 Helena Gao 密切协作。乐评逐曲讨论了“Pretty Ugly”“Midnight Sun”“Blue Moon”“Girl’s Girl”“Ambition”等歌的主题，包括女性愤怒、夜色浪漫、道德冲突和夸张野心。文章认为，每首歌都源自她真实的生活体验，并通过朗朗上口的旋律和精致流行制作呈现，使专辑既具派对感，又保持真诚与共鸣。

这篇 Rolling Stone 特写文章从职业生涯的角度讨论 Zara Larsson，并将《Midnight Sun》描述为她 2025 年发行的第五张专辑，也是巩固其流行地位的关键作品。文章以歌曲“The Ambition”的歌词为线索，强调专辑围绕她对流行成功的渴望、不满足感和争取长久影响力的心态展开。报道回顾了她此前的代表作，并指出《Midnight Sun》时期标志着她当前的走红与上升阶段，体现出她以长远性和在流行史上留下印记为核心的创作理念。
Melodic Mag 的评测标题即称《Midnight Sun》是 Zara Larsson 迄今为止最好的作品集，整体评价高度正面。摘要中提到，该专辑以 trance 风格启发的制作和她具有催眠感的歌声，将听众带入一个不愿醒来的阳光梦境，突出其梦幻且夏日化的音色与制作氛围。
Rolling Stone 官方 X 帐号发布的一则社交媒体帖子简要概括了他们对《Midnight Sun》的专辑评测观点，称可以听到 Zara Larsson 在这张专辑中“coming into her own”，即在艺术风格和流行定位上愈发成熟，并指出即便她较为公式化的片段也依然闪耀。
Musicboard 上用户“swaeze”的评论以高度主观的口吻描述《Midnight Sun》，认为这张专辑像是 Zara Larsson 命中注定要制作的唱片，将其形容为一张光滑、明亮的 dance-pop 作品，捕捉了夏天不仅作为季节，也作为一种情绪和体验的感觉。
Album of the Year 的页面汇总了《Midnight Sun》的各类评论与评分，并在摘要中引用了一段负面评价，称该专辑只是一次试图打造慵懒性感夏日流行专辑的尝试，发行时间略晚，而且在每一次尝试中都未命中目标，提示了相较主流正面评价的一种批评性视角。
Beatroutemedia 的文章以强烈的喜爱口吻讨论《Midnight Sun》，强调每首歌在制作和情感层面都经过精心雕琢，从明亮而响亮的制作到核心真挚的情感，认为这张专辑不仅仅是一张夏日专辑，而是兼具精致制作和真情流露的完整作品。

title: Lead
content: "Midnight Sun" is a studio album by Swedish singer Zara Larsson, released in 2025 through Epic Records and Sony Music. It follows her 2024 album "VENUS" and continues her work in upbeat dance-pop and electropop. The record was promoted as capturing the feeling of long Scandinavian summer days and nights, pairing high-energy pop production with lyrics about ambition, romance and emotional volatility. Upon release it received generally positive reviews from music critics for its energetic sound and Larsson's vocal performances, though at least one review criticized it as a formulaic attempt at summer pop. [1][2][3][4][11][24][25][28][15][16][17][18][33][34][36][38][39][40]

title: Background and development
content:
Before "Midnight Sun", Zara Larsson released several studio projects including "1" (2014), "So Good" (2017) and "VENUS" (2024), establishing herself as a mainstream pop artist with a focus on dance-pop and electronic-leaning production. [27][28][29][30]

Epic Records listed "Midnight Sun" as a 2025 CD album release by Zara Larsson, confirming its issue through the label and associating it with Sony Music's Epic imprint. [3][4][5][21][23][24]

A Sony Music Canada press release announced that Zara Larsson had released her new album "Midnight Sun", presenting it as a major pop project and part of her ongoing collaboration with Epic Records and Sony Music. [11][24]

In interviews around the album cycle, Larsson described the "Midnight Sun" era as tied to her long-standing ambition to be a leading pop artist, speaking about wanting the number-one spot and to leave an identifiable mark on pop history. [15][20][35]

A profile in The Fader quoted lyrics from the song "The Ambition" in which Larsson sings about wanting success so much that "everything's a competition", framing the album as a document of her drive and anxieties about pop stardom. [15][33][35]

title: Composition and themes
content:
Critics commonly describe "Midnight Sun" as a high-energy dance-pop album that rarely slows down, emphasizing uptempo beats, trance-inspired textures and glossy electronic production. [25][33][34][36]

Rolling Stone called the album a "high-energy dance-pop" record that "refuses to ever slow down" and sustains a summer atmosphere of "good vibes, long days, and late nights" across its running time. [33]

EUPHORIA. characterized the ten-track set as an "ultimate party record" with enough energy and zest to make listeners want to dance "anytime, anywhere". [34]

The album incorporates diverse influences including trance, Brazilian funk and ballroom, which reviewers link to Larsson's youthful energy and artistic growth. [16][34]

Several songs explore themes of ambition, self-confidence and emotional volatility; The Fader and Rolling Stone highlight "The Ambition" as a central track in which Larsson sings about wanting to be number one and feeling that everything is a competition. [15][33][35]

Rolling Stone groups songs such as "Midnight Sun", "Blue Moon", "Euro Summer" and "Puss Puss" as depicting sweetness and tender scenes like short skirts, late-night calls and lovers' handprints, while also noting darker or "messier" emotional moments where Larsson portrays jealousy and anger. [33]

The track "Pretty Ugly" is repeatedly singled out for its portrayal of female anger; Rolling Stone describes it as built on a stomp beat with lyrics about keying and crashing a car, while EUPHORIA. calls it an electro-influenced lead single that turns "female rage" into a powerful force. [33][34]

EUPHORIA. notes that across the album Larsson uses these sounds to represent her youthful energy, growth and ambition, with each song presented as an experience drawn from her own life. [34]

Melodic Mag writes that the album's trance-inspired production and Larsson's "hypnotizing" voice create a dreamy, sun-soaked atmosphere, describing the listening experience as being transported into a sunny dream. [36]

title: Release and promotion
content:
MusicBrainz lists "Midnight Sun" as a 2025 Zara Larsson release in the album category, grouping several physical and digital editions. [1][2]

Discogs documents multiple 2025 CD editions of "Midnight Sun", including standard and signed versions released through Epic Records, indicating a coordinated physical rollout. [3][4][5][21][23][24]

An Epic Records product page promotes the "Midnight Sun" CD with album artwork and purchasing options, aligning it with the label's roster of mainstream pop releases. [24]

Sony Music Canada's press release announcing the album frames it as a significant new release in Larsson's career and part of her partnership with Epic and Sony Music. [11]

Media coverage around the album's launch, including pieces in The Fader, i-D and other outlets, presented the "Midnight Sun" era as a pivotal moment in Larsson's ascent to international pop stardom. [15][19][20][35]

title: Critical reception
content:
"Midnight Sun" received generally positive reviews from music critics, with praise focusing on its high-energy pop production, summery atmosphere and Larsson's vocal performances, though some criticism targeted its formulaic tendencies and timing as a summer release. [25][33][34][36][38][39][40]

Rolling Stone's review calls the album a high-energy dance-pop record that keeps a summer mood of "good vibes, long days, and late nights", and concludes that Larsson is "coming into her own" on the project, with even its more formulaic moments shining brightly. [33][37]

EUPHORIA. describes "Midnight Sun" as "the ultimate party record" and highlights tracks such as "Pretty Ugly" and "Blue Moon" for their energetic, feel-good qualities, noting the album's diverse sonic palette and depiction of youth and ambition. [34]

Melodic Mag argues that "Midnight Sun" is Larsson's "best body of work yet", praising its trance-inspired production, cohesive mood and her "hypnotizing" vocals. [36]

An article on Beatroutemedia states that every song on the album feels carefully crafted, from its bright, loud production to the genuine, heartfelt emotions at its core. [40]

User-oriented platforms also reflect enthusiasm; a Musicboard review describes the record as a sleek, radiant dance-pop album that captures summer as both a season and a state of mind, and suggests it feels like the album Larsson was destined to make. [38]

In contrast, a review aggregated by Album of the Year criticizes "Midnight Sun" as "merely an attempt at a sultry summer pop album" released "about two months too late" and claims it misses every shot it takes, illustrating a more negative critical perspective. [39]

A feature in The Fader interprets the album as a key document of Larsson's ambition and desire for longevity in pop, arguing that her current ascent to stardom is closely tied to the artistic persona presented on "Midnight Sun". [15][35]
